findings.title: join() skips terminate() for remaining flusher processes when the deadline expires
findings.body: In SpanFlusher.join(), the loop over self.processes breaks out entirely when the deadline is exhausted, so any processes after the one being waited on are never sent terminate(). The previous single-process implementation always called process.terminate() after the wait loop, guaranteeing the old flusher was killed at the deadline. With multiple processes, if an earlier process consumes the remaining time (e.g. it is blocked in a Kafka future.result() wait), the later processes are left running. Since close() deliberately does not stop flushers and join() is the only shutdown point, on a rebalance the leftover processes can overlap with the newly created SpanFlusher's processes for the same shards, causing two flushers to flush the same shard queues concurrently (duplicate segments produced to the buffered-segments topic), and a process hung in produce can leak indefinitely. After the while-wait, terminate() should be called for every remaining process rather than breaking.

findings.title: max_processes=0 is silently treated as 'one process per shard', negative values disable flushing
findings.body: self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards) conflates an explicit 0 with None: an operator passing --flusher-processes 0 (the click option accepts any int, no range validation) gets 0 or len(shards), i.e. the maximum fan-out of one process per shard instead of zero/one. Conversely a negative value survives the 'or' (truthy), making num_processes = min(negative, shards) negative, so range(num_processes) is empty and no flusher process is created at all — the consumer would keep writing spans to Redis with nothing ever flushing them, with no error surfaced. Consider explicit validation (e.g. click.IntRange(1, ...)) and treating only None as unset.

findings.title: Inconsistent metrics tag keys: 'shard' vs 'shards', and multi-shard values under the 'shard' tag
findings.body: In SpanFlusher.main(), the 'spans.buffer.flusher.produce' and 'spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes' metrics are tagged with 'shard' while 'spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce' is tagged with 'shards'. Additionally, when max_processes < number of shards, shard_tag is a comma-joined list like '0,2,4', so the 'shard' tag no longer contains a single shard id. This makes dashboards/alerts grouped by shard inconsistent across these related metrics and breaks any existing per-shard aggregation on the 'shard' tag for these series.

findings.title: _create_process_for_shard is dead code left over from the refactor
findings.body: SpanFlusher._create_process_for_shard(shard) is never called anywhere — restarts go through _ensure_processes_alive, which calls _create_process_for_shards(process_index, shards) directly. The unused method suggests a per-shard restart granularity that does not exist (restarting always recreates the whole process and all its shards), which is misleading for future maintainers. It should be removed.

findings.title: test_basic relies on a fixed 0.1s sleep for the flusher thread to produce
findings.body: The newly added 'step.poll(); time.sleep(0.1)' before step.join() is a timing race: the test asserts exactly one produced message, but the background flusher thread must observe current_drift, call flush_segments against real Redis, and append the message within that wall-clock window. join() sets stopped.value before waiting, so a flush that hasn't happened by then will never occur. On a loaded or slow CI runner where the thread isn't scheduled within 100ms, '(msg,) = messages' will fail intermittently. A poll/wait loop on len(messages) with a timeout would make this deterministic.
